**A dsh plugin: a turn-end quality check. When the turn edited code or config files, the checks the
project itself declares run before the turn closes; a failure is sent back as a repair instruction t
hat opens a new turn, with a cap on injections per session and a cap on total running time.**

##  What it does
- **At turn end, not while the turn runs.** The hook is the host event `agent/turn-stopping`: read t
his session's **successful** edits → walk each file up to the nearest directory that has a manifest
→ decide which check applies → run it. A failure is sent back through `agent.followup`; the host sti

ll checks the inbox after turn-stopping, so a repair instruction opens a new turn.
- **One run has e
xactly three outcomes**: `pass` (it really finished with exit 0), `code-failure` (it ran and reporte
d code errors), `not-run` (it never ran). A check that did not truly finish is never recorded as pas
sed, and "could not run" is never mixed up with "code error" — the first sends "please confirm manua

lly", writes no memory and never reaches the lesson bus as `gate-failure`.
- **Only commands the pro
ject itself declares.** One of four whitelisted commands per root; with no declaration no command is
issued — no check is better than an invented command that fails every time (see "The four check com

mands").
- **Keeps a repair loop from running away.** Repair injections are counted per session acro
ss turns; once the count is used up, one user-visible release note is sent and auto-repair stops. To
tal running time is capped; a timeout is sent as "could not run" rather than passing without a word.
- **It does not edit code, does not block dangerous commands (that is danger-guard's job) and does
not write any file.**
##  Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Remove with `dsh plugin --profile web remove @jayyuen66/dsh-quality-gate`. The package is on the pub
lic npm registry, so installation needs no credentials.
- **Requires Node.js `>= 24.9`.** The artifacts use newer runtime features such as `AbortSignal.any`

.
- **Requires a host `dsh` on the `0.2.1-rc.5` or `0.2.2-alpha.3` line.** The requirement the host
reads is `engines.dsh` (`^0.2.1-rc.5 || ^0.2.2-alpha.3`), and it **decides compatibility on its own*
*; pre-release versions participate in range comparison, and `0.3.0` and later need the explicit ris

k-accepting grant `dsh plugin --profile

allow-version @ --dsh-version --accept
-risk`. The support window rolls: this package is verified against every released host version insid
e the window at publish time and re-verified once the window moves, so the version numbers in this b

ullet are not a standing promise.
- **The runtime dependency `@jayyuen66/dsh-plugin-shared` must alr

eady be on the same registry**, otherwise the whole set 404s.
[该节后续省略]

[该节后续省略]
##  Verify it is working
1. **The layer is mounted.** `dsh --profile web --dump-config` ends with `# == @jayyuen66/dsh-qualit

y-gate` plus `- id: quality-gate`.
[该节后续省略]
##  What it does not provide
- **No model tools.** The whole implementation is the `agent/turn-stopping` listener; there is no `g

ate_status` tool to call.
- **No HTTP routes and no Remote namespace.** The settings card uses the o
fficial `configForms` form and writes through the host's channel — unlike plugins that ship their ow

n data endpoints, the only data this package holds is its settings.
- **No CLI subcommand.**
- **No
file writes, no telemetry**; the only outbound request is the memory gateway you explicitly enable (

see "Data and privacy").
- Things it uses when available: the `lessonLoop` bus (lesson reports), `cr
edentials` (key resolution), `sandboxPolicy` (per-session policy), `sessionQuery` (event reads), `sh
ell` (running commands). All are optional `ctx.get` reads — if one is missing, only that capability
is gone; the plugin still loads.
##  Data and privacy
| Item | Facts |
| Nothing leaves by default | `memoryFeedback` off plus an empty URL are two independent guards — wi

th either empty, nothing is sent and the credential store is not even queried |
| What leaves the ma
chine | When enabled, only the command, the project root and the full error text (folded onto one li

ne, not truncated) — sent to **the gateway you configured** |
| URL and credential safety | Credenti
als go to `https` or loopback addresses only (`127.0.0.0/8`, IPv6 loopback, `localhost`); `localhost
` depends on the local hosts file and DNS, and is a deliberate exception — if hosts points elsewhere
, credentials go there. Plain `http` to a non-loopback host is refused as unconfigured, with the rea
son stated. A base URL that does not parse as a valid `http(s)` URL also counts as unconfigured; URL

s with userinfo are rejected |
| The key | The value lives in the host credential service (a credent
ials file under `$DSH_HOME`); settings store only the reference name, and a name that is not a valid

POSIX variable name counts as unconfigured |
| Failure handling | A failed push only warns and neve
r blocks the turn end: missing configuration or an unsafe URL is reported once per load; HTTP non-2x
x, timeouts and send errors are logged every time they happen (collapsing them would hide a persiste

nt fault) |
| File reads | Whether manifests exist, the root `package.json` scripts, `pyproject.toml
` section headers, the start of a truncated output file written to disk; no file writes, no telemetr

y |
| Memory | Per-session state (edit records, injection count, event cursors) lives in process mem
ory and is cleared when the plugin unloads |
